column2: How can a hormone value be abnormal without gland hypersecretion, or normal despite disease?
column3: Concentration integrates secretion, pulsatility, binding, distribution, conversion, degradation and clearance, and effect depends on receptor abundance and sensitivity, so normal levels can coexist with resistance.

column2: Why is endocrine physiology tissue-specific as well as systemic?
column3: Local enzymes alter hormone action within tissues: deiodinases activate or inactivate thyroid hormone, 11-beta hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase controls cortisol access to mineralocorticoid receptors, and aromatase makes oestrogens from androgens.

column2: When is a trophic hormone within the reference range still abnormal, and when does a non-suppressed one need confirmation?
column3: It is pathological when the target is clearly deficient. With a high target, a non-suppressed trophic value raises assay interference, resistance or autonomous central secretion, confirmed before imaging.
